text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Three Slovaks kidnapped last October in Ingushetia, near Chechnya, are expected to be released soon.
- Czech car maker Skoda ranked first in sales in Slovakia last year, selling 23,035 cars. Skoda said it planned to increase exports to Slovakia to 25,000 units in 1997.

- Skoda imported components, mainly steel sheets from VSZ and tyres from Matador Puchov, worth about three billion crowns in Slovakia last year, and said it planned to increase deliveries to 3.8 billion crowns in 1997.

- Czech parliamentary chairman Milos Zeman will pay a two- day visit to Slovakia, starting on January 15. Zeman is scheduled to meet his Slovak counterpart Ivan Gasparovic, President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Acceleration of the trade deficit in November and the expected surge in imports at the end of the year are expected to push the total shortfall beyond the forecasted 52 billion crowns for 1996.
- Overall investment to hydro projects, including planned river dams, are expected to total 3.7 billion crowns this year.
- Slovakia and Ukraine have so far created 200 joint- venture companies.
- Heavy engineering company Povazske Strojarne said it planned to widen its sales network abroad, mainly towards western Europe, from its current sales offices in Russia, Romania and Bulgaria.
SME - Transport Minister Alexander Rezes said he was considering resigning in the near future.

- The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) opposed attempts of other opposition parties to initiate a referendum to change the presidential electoral system to a direct citizen vote. The SDL said that such a change would be unconstitutional and that it might bring the case to the constitutional court.
